investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T17:01–17:09Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pod remained Unschedulable for 128–146 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and violating all four required-evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector for remote-agent pods. With 0 available slots on those 2 nodes and 4 nodes excluded by affinity rules, no scheduling path exists and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims are present. The pod never starts, so the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never receives an agent identity or VM assignment, leaving all required evidence fields empty and causing the check to fail before any contract assertion can be evaluated.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes may have had labels removed or the pod spec's affinity rules may have been tightened, shrinking the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.

Tertiary — VM peer-pod provider quota or infrastructure limit: the underlying peer-pod provider (e.g., cloud VM quota) may have hit an external cap that prevents the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource from being replenished even if pods are deleted.

Lower probability — eval runner scheduling a burst of concurrent remote-agent probes (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime all ran within the same ~7-minute window) that collectively exhausted remaining VM slots before any single probe could complete.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T17:01–17:09Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pod remained Unschedulable for 128–146 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and violating all four required-evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector for remote-agent pods. With 0 available slots on those 2 nodes and 4 nodes excluded by affinity rules, no scheduling path exists and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims are present. The pod never starts, so the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never receives an agent identity or VM assignment, leaving all required evidence fields empty and causing the check to fail before any contract assertion can be evaluated.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes may have had labels removed or the pod spec's affinity rules may have been tightened, shrinking the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.

Lower probability — eval runner scheduling a burst of concurrent remote-agent probes (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime all ran within the same ~7-minute window) that collectively exhausted remaining VM slots before any single probe could complete.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-07 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the 6-node cluster has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure and production Kubernetes cluster resource failure localized to the remote-agents swarm scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" — present identically across all three sibling checks — confirms that every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod failed at the Kubernetes scheduling layer before any agent process started. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) timed out after ~128–152 seconds per check, returning no evidence and causing all three checks to fail their expected-output contracts.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary: Node affinity or node selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, meaning the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability. The scheduler message '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' confirms this constraint is active.

Tertiary: A surge in concurrent remote agent workloads (from users, other evals, or background jobs) may have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before the eval run began, leaving no headroom for the eval's own pods.

Lower confidence: A node running kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads may have become unhealthy or cordoned, reducing effective VM capacity below the normal baseline without the remaining node(s) being able to absorb the load.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and unallocated on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission failure would need to be investigated.

If the pod scheduling error message were absent from a re-run and the pod reached Running state but the agent returned no evidence, the root cause would shift to an application-layer failure (e.g., agent startup crash, API auth error, or response format mismatch) rather than a scheduling resource constraint.
If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the failure would be localized to the runtime eval path rather than the shared scheduling layer.

If the 4 non-kata nodes were shown to have matching node affinity labels and sufficient general resources, the node affinity constraint hypothesis would be disproved and the failure would be purely a kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity issue on all 6 nodes.

If a passing run of any remote-agents check were found in history (lastPassingAt is currently null due to previousRunCount=0), it would establish a baseline and help determine whether this is a new regression or a persistent capacity ceiling.
followUpEvals: Add a preflight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a clear capacity signal rather than waiting for a scheduling timeout.

Add a dedicated eval that monitors the count of Pending remote agent pods and alerts if any pod remains unscheduled for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60 seconds), enabling earlier detection of capacity exhaustion.

Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote agent pods (in Pending or Terminating state) remain after each eval run cycle, catching cases where withCleanup does not fire on scheduling failure.

Extend the remote-agent-create check to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerMessage, unschedulableReason) so future failures produce actionable evidence rather than an empty evidence object.
